meta_desc: Class 8 Area worksheet (Ganita Prakash Part 2, Chapter 7): area of triangles, parallelograms, trapeziums, rhombuses, kites and composite shapes. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Triangle ½bh, parallelogram bh, trapezium ½(a + b)h
key_sub: Rhombus and kite: ½ × product of the diagonals.
body_html:
How it works

Parallelogram: base × perpendicular height. Triangle: ½ × base × height.

Trapezium: ½ × (sum of the parallel sides) × height. Rhombus and kite: ½ × d1 × d2.

For a composite shape, split it into rectangles and triangles and add (or subtract a hole).

Example

Find the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 8 cm and 12 cm and height 5 cm.

½ × (8 + 12) × 5

Answer: 50 cm²

Example

The diagonals of a kite are 10 cm and 7 cm. Find its area.

½ × 10 × 7

Answer: 35 cm²

Common mistakes

  • Using the slant side instead of the perpendicular height.
  • Forgetting the ½ for a triangle.
  • Multiplying the diagonals of a rhombus without halving.

faq.q: How do you find the area of a trapezium?
faq.a: Half the sum of the parallel sides times the perpendicular distance between them.

faq.q: How do you find the area of a rhombus?
faq.a: Half the product of its diagonals, because the diagonals cut it into four right triangles.

faq.q: Why is the area of a triangle half of base × height?
faq.a: Two copies of the triangle make a parallelogram with the same base and height.
